newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore economic '97 growth at 7.2 pct - economist.
newsitem.headline: Singapore economic '97 growth at 7.2 pct - economist.

text.p: Economists from the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) were more bullish than the Singapore government in forecasts for the economy, projecting 7.2 percent growth this year, state television reported on Friday.
NTU's Econometric Modelling Unit put Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP) growth at 7.2 percent this year and 7.8 percent for 1998.
This was stronger etween 5-7 percent. Singapore's economy registered 6.5 percent growth in 1996.
NTU's economists attributed the stronger GDP growth to synchronised growth for all major economic sectors, low inflation worldwide and a Singapore dollar that was unlikely to strengthen.
